one_month_reasoning: Avnet's Q1 FY27 report most likely comes on Wed Nov 4, after the window, which is marked at the Fri Oct 30 close. The supervisor confirmed this on EDGAR: 11 straight fiscal Q1-Q3 earnings 8-Ks came exactly 32 days after the Saturday quarter-end, and Q1 ends Oct 3. I put about 10% on the report landing inside the window. Arrow's Q3 has also moved later (~Nov 5). The window therefore holds only read-across: TI and other analog/MCU suppliers' Q3 reports, memory price updates and ECIA data. I centre on today's $106.94 with no drift; momentum after an all-time-high close roughly offsets short-term reversal. The distribution is a mixture: 85% lognormal at 10% monthly sigma (37%/3.5 = 10.6%) and 15% at 16% sigma, which covers the small chance of an in-window print and peer-driven tail moves. That is tighter than my round-1 11.5% sigma.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods: forward P/E (~$11.85 NTM EPS at Oct-2027 on ~86M diluted shares x 9x = $107, weight 0.5); mid-cycle earnings power (~$7.35 x 13x = $95, weight 0.3); and the historical peak-cycle multiple on the Q1 FY27 run-rate restated to 86M shares ($11.27 x 6.5x = $73, weight 0.2). Result is about $97.

inputs_detail.derivation: 82.07M basic (10-K cover) plus awards (Q4 diluted 84.69M) plus ~3.2M net shares from the cash-principal 1.75% 2030 convert (conversion ~$70.27) at $107. No Q4 buybacks. Dilution rises if the stock rises.
FY27: $10.45 (MarketBeat) to $10.57 (stockanalysis, 3 analysts). Thin coverage that lags the guide run-rate.
The Q1 guide run-rate restated to 86M shares is $11.27 ($2.85 x 4 x 85/86). Add ~5% for backlog into 1H27 and book-to-bill above 1 at Arrow, capped because NAND loosens in 2H27.

AVT trades at ~10x forward consensus today. At the FY22-23 peak it traded at ~6x adjusted EPS (2022-23 monthly highs $48-51 on FY23 adj EPS $8.06; the Oct-2022 low of $35.9 was ~4.5x). I verified these against EDGAR XBRL EPS and Twelve Data prices. A year further into the upcycle I expect partial compression, not a full move to the peak-cycle norm, given 10-15% AI/data-center exposure.

Reported debt at Jun 27, 2026 was $3,212.8M and net debt $3.06B. Debt is likely somewhat higher through the working-capital build, at ~7% all-in. Tax is the midpoint of the 21-25% guide.

Normalized-earnings multiples for distributors sit around 10-15x. Arrow's 5-year average is ~9.6x on mixed earnings and its high is 15.5x. AVT traded at ~13-17x the trough-ish FY19/FY21 GAAP EPS of $1.59-1.93 (EDGAR).

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Peak-cycle base rate: Q1 FY27 run-rate restated to 86M shares, $11.27 x 6.5x

inputs_detail.derivation: FY23 adjusted EPS was $8.06 (GAAP $8.26). The 2022-23 monthly highs of $48-51 (Twelve Data) put the peak multiple at ~6.0-6.3x adjusted. FY22 GAAP EPS of $6.94 gives ~7x on the 2022 high of $50. I use 6.5x, the midpoint.

bear.story: The cycle peaks in mid-2027, as distributor upcycles typically do about 6-8 quarters after the trough. NAND loosens in 2H27, price-driven revenue reverses, and customers' double-ordering unwinds. A 2027 GDP recession (Kalshi ~22%) would deepen it. The market applies the historical ~6x peak multiple to ~$11 EPS, giving ~$65.

base.story: EPS rises toward a $12 run-rate through FY27, helped by backlog into 1H27, but late-cycle risk compresses the multiple from ~10x to ~8.5-9x forward on ~86M diluted shares. The stock ends roughly flat.

bull.story: The AI and memory supercycle runs into 2028, with DRAM tight through 2027 per TrendForce. EPS reaches a $14-15 run-rate, and the market holds ~10x on a structurally longer cycle.

thesis_break_reason: $70 is ~6.2x the $11.27 Q1-guide run-rate (on 86M shares), the multiple Avnet traded at on FY23 peak adjusted EPS of $8.06 (verified against EDGAR EPS and Twelve Data prices). Trading there would most likely mean the market has decided earnings have peaked: book-to-bill below 1, a sequential guide-down, a memory price reversal or an order unwind. A ~35% drop is more than 1 sigma at 37% vol, not ordinary noise.

reasoning: Round 2. The facts the supervisor established mostly confirmed my round-1 inputs, and three changes follow. (1) I verified the Kalshi 2027 recession market at the source: the Kalshi API for KXRECSSNBER-27 shows last trade 22c (bid 20 / ask 22), $542k volume and 275k open interest. My round-1 ~41% from an aggregator snippet was wrong, so the bear weight goes from 30% back to 25%. Note that the market's definition is two negative GDP quarters, which is not NBER. (2) Diluted shares are ~86M, not 84-85M. There were no Q4 buybacks, and the cash-principal convert adds ~3.2M net shares at $107. That cuts per-share values ~1-2%. (3) FY23 peak EPS of $8.26 is GAAP; adjusted was $8.06. I verified both against EDGAR XBRL (FY22 $6.94, FY23 $8.26, FY24 $5.43, FY25 $2.75, FY26 $4.01 GAAP) and Twelve Data monthly prices (2022-23 highs $48-51, Oct-2022 low $35.9). The peak multiple was ~6x adjusted, so the base rate holds. Avnet's GAAP EPS fell 34% in FY24 and another 49% in FY25 after the peak, a reminder of how hard distributor earnings fall after a cycle top. The earnings-date fact (~Nov 4) matches my round-1 call. Fair value moves from $98 to $97 on the share count. The scenario mean rises from ~$106 to ~$107 because of the lower bear weight. The median is ~$104, and the ladder shifts up ~1-2 points from round 1 in the 64-128 range. I keep my own 20% weight on the historical peak multiple, which the supervisor flagged as a judgment disagreement. It is the clearest base rate in my lane: every prior AVT cycle top (2018, 2022-23) traded at ~6-7x peak EPS, and the stock never held above ~$55 through 2016-2025.
